class.name: Box3DCollisionShape
class.brief_description: One shape of a compound [Box3DBody]. Add as a child of the body.
class.description: One shape of a compound [Box3DBody]. Add these as children of a body to give it several shapes at different local transforms -- a table top plus four legs, a barrel plus its lid. As soon as a body has at least one Box3DCollisionShape child, the body's own [member Box3DBody.shape_type] is ignored and only the children are used. Each child carries its own [member density], [member friction] and [member restitution], so a compound can mix materials. Most properties here apply to the live shape: the sizes resize it in place, and the surface material, filter and event properties are pushed straight to the solver. Only a [member shape_type] change, or a property changed before the body exists, rebuilds the parent body's shapes -- which matters because a rebuild drops the contacts and the warm-start impulses that were holding a stack together.

method.name: are_contact_events_enabled
method.description: Whether the solver is currently reporting contact events for this shape: [member contact_events] resolved against the parent body, after Box3D's own rules. [code]false[/code] when there is no live shape. Read this rather than [member contact_events] when the question is "will I get an event", since [constant EVENT_INHERIT] does not say on its own.

method.name: are_hit_events_enabled
method.description: Whether the solver is currently reporting hit events for this shape: [member hit_events] resolved against the parent body. [code]false[/code] when there is no live shape.

method.name: are_sensor_events_enabled
method.description: Whether the solver is currently reporting sensor overlap events for this shape: [member sensor_events] resolved against the parent body, after Box3D's own rules (it ignores sensor events on shapes that are not sensors). [code]false[/code] when there is no live shape.

method.name: compute_mass_data
method.description: The mass this shape contributes, as a [Dictionary] with [code]mass[/code] ([float]), [code]center[/code] ([Vector3]) and [code]inertia[/code] ([Basis]) -- the per-shape breakdown behind a compound body's total.

method.name: get_aabb
method.description: This shape's world-space bounding box, as the broad phase holds it.

method.name: get_body
method.description: The [Box3DBody] the solver holds this shape against, or [code]null[/code] when there is no live shape. This is what Box3D knows, not this node's parent: it is the answer for a shape that arrived in a query result or a contact event, where the node's own parentage is not the question being asked.

method.name: get_capsule
method.description: The live capsule geometry as a [Dictionary] with [code]center1[/code] and [code]center2[/code] ([Vector3], the two end-cap centres in the parent body's local space) and [code]radius[/code] ([float], metres). A capsule is defined by its two centres, not by a height and an axis, so its total length is [code]center1.distance_to(center2) + 2 * radius[/code]. Empty unless [method get_geometry_type] is [constant GEOMETRY_CAPSULE].

method.name: get_closest_point
method.description: The point on this shape's surface closest to [param target], in world space.

method.name: get_filter
method.description: The filter the [b]solver[/b] holds for this shape, as a [Dictionary] with [code]layer[/code], [code]mask[/code], [code]layer_high[/code], [code]mask_high[/code] and [code]group[/code]. That is this node's own filter while [member filter_override] is on, and the parent body's filter otherwise -- which makes it the way to confirm that an override took. Empty when there is no live shape.

method.name: get_geometry_type
method.description: What the solver actually holds for this shape, as a [enum GeometryType] value. This is [b]not[/b] [member shape_type]: [member shape_type] is what you authored, and Box3D has no box, cylinder or cone primitive, so all three come back as [constant GEOMETRY_HULL]. Check this before calling [method get_sphere], [method get_capsule], [method get_hull] or [method get_mesh], each of which returns an empty [Dictionary] for the wrong geometry. Returns [constant GEOMETRY_NONE] until the parent body has built its shapes in a running [Box3DWorld].

method.name: get_hull
method.description: The live convex hull as a [Dictionary]: [code]points[/code] ([PackedVector3Array], the hull vertices in the parent body's local space), [code]center[/code] ([Vector3]), [code]aabb[/code] ([AABB]), [code]volume[/code] ([float]), [code]surface_area[/code] ([float]), [code]inner_radius[/code] ([float], the largest sphere that fits inside), [code]vertex_count[/code] and [code]face_count[/code] ([int]). This is the geometry Box3D actually built, [b]after[/b] hulling: the points are the hull's own vertices, not the ones handed in, and there are fewer of them than you supplied whenever some fell inside. Empty unless [method get_geometry_type] is [constant GEOMETRY_HULL], which covers box, cylinder and cone shapes as well as hulls.

method.name: get_mesh
method.description: The live triangle mesh as a [Dictionary] with [code]scale[/code] ([Vector3]), [code]vertex_count[/code], [code]triangle_count[/code] and [code]material_count[/code] ([int]). Counts and scale only -- the geometry itself stays in Box3D. Empty unless [method get_geometry_type] is [constant GEOMETRY_MESH], which this node gets from [method set_mesh], or from a query or event payload naming a body's own mesh collider. The [member shape_type] property cannot author one.

method.name: get_shape_name
method.description: The debug name set by [method set_shape_name].

method.name: get_sphere
method.description: The live sphere geometry as a [Dictionary] with [code]center[/code] ([Vector3], in the parent body's local space) and [code]radius[/code] ([float], metres). Empty unless [method get_geometry_type] is [constant GEOMETRY_SPHERE]. This reads what the solver holds, which is what [method set_sphere] may have changed since the node's own properties were authored.

method.name: get_world
method.description: The [Box3DWorld] simulating this shape, or [code]null[/code] when there is no live shape. Read from the solver, like [method get_body], rather than by walking up the scene tree.

method.name: is_sensor
method.description: Whether this shape is a trigger volume rather than a solid one. Inherited from the parent body's [member Box3DBody.is_sensor].

method.name: is_shape_valid
method.description: Whether the shape exists in the solver yet. It is created with the parent body, so this is [code]false[/code] until the body is in a running [Box3DWorld].

method.name: raycast
method.description: Casts a ray against [b]this shape alone[/b], ignoring the rest of the world, and returns the result as a [Dictionary]. [param origin] is a world-space position and [param translation] is the full ray vector from it (its length is the ray's length), not a target point -- unlike [method Box3DWorld.raycast], which takes a from and a to. The result carries [code]hit[/code] ([bool]), [code]point[/code] ([Vector3]), [code]normal[/code] ([Vector3]), [code]fraction[/code] ([float], 0..1 along [param translation]), [code]triangle_index[/code], [code]child_index[/code], [code]material_index[/code] and [code]iterations[/code] ([int], how much work the solver did, a diagnostic). The geometry fields are only meaningful when [code]hit[/code] is [code]true[/code]. Use it when you already know which shape you care about -- verifying an aim point, re-testing a hit reported by an event -- since it skips the broad phase entirely.

method.name: set_capsule
method.description: Replaces this shape's capsule geometry in the solver, without rebuilding the body. [param center1] and [param center2] are the end-cap centres in the parent body's local space, [param radius] is in metres; the capsule's axis is whatever line those two centres describe. Same live-edit semantics as [method set_sphere]: the node's [member capsule_radius] and [member capsule_height] are untouched, and a body rebuild reverts to them. See [method set_sphere] for [param update_mass]. Does nothing unless [method get_geometry_type] is [constant GEOMETRY_CAPSULE].

method.name: set_hull
method.description: Rebuilds this shape's convex hull from [param points], given in the parent body's local space, without rebuilding the body. [b]The points are hulled, not used verbatim[/b]: any that fall inside the hull are dropped, so [method get_hull] afterwards reports fewer vertices than you passed. At least 4 points are required (fewer enclose no volume) and at most 255 are kept. A degenerate set -- all collinear, all coplanar -- builds no hull and leaves the shape as it was, with a warning. Same live-edit semantics as [method set_sphere]: node properties are untouched and a body rebuild reverts. See [method set_sphere] for [param update_mass]. Does nothing unless [method get_geometry_type] is [constant GEOMETRY_HULL].

method.name: set_mesh
method.description: Retypes this shape into a triangle mesh built from [param vertices] and [param indices], at [param scale]. Returns [code]false[/code], having changed nothing, when the data does not describe a mesh: an index count that is not a multiple of three, an index outside [param vertices], or a scale that is zero or not finite. [b]Winding is Box3D's, not Godot's[/b] (counter-clockwise by the right-hand rule) and passes through untouched, exactly as [member Box3DBody.mesh_indices] does. Mesh collision is one-sided, so indices lifted straight from a Godot [Mesh] give a collider that is not solid from the side you expect. A triangle mesh only generates contacts on a static body or a sensor, so this warns on anything else. [param update_mass] defaults to [code]false[/code] here, unlike [method set_sphere] and its two siblings: a mesh has no volume, so recomputing the body's mass from a lone mesh shape would leave it with none. Pass [code]true[/code] only when the body has other shapes to weigh. Same live-edit semantics as [method set_sphere] -- the node's authored properties are untouched and a rebuild of the body's shapes reverts to them. This node holds the mesh data for as long as the shape does, and frees it when the shape goes or another [method set_mesh] replaces it.

method.name: set_mesh_scale
method.description: Rescales the mesh this shape already holds, keeping its triangles. Returns [code]false[/code] when the shape is not a mesh, or when [param scale] is zero or not finite. This is the only way to change a mesh collider's scale after it exists: node scale is baked into the geometry when the shape is built, and this scale is the one place Box3D lets it move afterwards.

method.name: set_shape_name
method.description: Sets a debug name for this shape, reported back by Box3D's own diagnostics.

method.name: set_sphere
method.description: Replaces this shape's sphere geometry in the solver, without rebuilding the body. [param center] is in the parent body's local space and [param radius] is in metres. Live geometry editing, for a shape that grows, shrinks or shifts during play. It does [b]not[/b] write back to [member sphere_radius]: the node's properties still describe what was authored, and a body rebuild (a [member shape_type] change, a new child shape) discards this and returns to them. [param update_mass] recomputes the parent body's mass, centre of mass and inertia from all its shapes afterwards. Leave it on unless you are changing several shapes at once, in which case pass [code]false[/code] for all but the last. Does nothing unless [method get_geometry_type] is [constant GEOMETRY_SPHERE].

members.member: Full extents of the [constant BOX] shape, in metres (not half-extents).
Total height of the [constant CAPSULE], [constant CYLINDER] and [constant CONE] shapes, in metres, end caps included.
Radius of the [constant CAPSULE], [constant CYLINDER] and [constant CONE] shapes, in metres.

Box3D's group index for this shape, honoured only while [member filter_override] is on. When it is not 0 it overrides the layer and mask bits entirely: two shapes in the same [b]positive[/b] group always collide, two in the same [b]negative[/b] group never do.
Which layers this shape is [b]on[/b], honoured only while [member filter_override] is on. Layers 1 to 32; see [member collision_layer_high] for the rest.
Collision layers 33 to 64 for this shape, honoured only while [member filter_override] is on. Box3D's filter is 64 bits wide while Godot's layer inspector is 32, so the upper half lives here.
Which layers this shape [b]scans[/b], honoured only while [member filter_override] is on. Two shapes collide when each one's mask includes a layer the other is on.
The scan half of [member collision_layer_high]: which of layers 33 to 64 this shape collides with. Honoured only while [member filter_override] is on.

Whether this shape reports contact events, as an [enum EventMode] tri-state. [constant EVENT_INHERIT] (the default) follows the parent body's [member Box3DBody.contact_monitor]; [constant EVENT_ENABLED] and [constant EVENT_DISABLED] decide it for this shape alone. That is how one child of a compound reports [signal Box3DBody.body_entered] without paying for events on the rest of it -- a trigger plate on a machine, say. [method are_contact_events_enabled] reads back what the solver actually holds.

Lets a [Box3DContactRules] never-collide rule see this shape's pairs. Only [b]one[/b] shape of a pair has to turn it on, so tagging the handful of shapes a rule applies to is enough. Off by default and [b]creation time[/b]: Box3D has no live setter for it, so changing it rebuilds the shape. Note that this gates [b]sensor overlaps[/b] too -- Box3D consults the same filter callback there, so a never-collide rule also hides the pair from sensors.
Mass per unit volume for this shape alone, in kg/m3. The parent body's mass is the sum over its shapes, so a compound can be deliberately bottom-heavy.

Whether changing this shape's filter also recomputes contacts that already exist, rather than only affecting pairs that move afterwards. On by default, because a widened mask that does nothing until something moves is a bug that is very hard to see. Upstream calls this almost as expensive as recreating the shape, so turn it off when a filter is changed every frame and a frame of latency is acceptable.

Turn on to give this shape its own collision filter instead of inheriting the parent [Box3DBody]'s. Off by default: a child shape's default layer and mask would otherwise silently override the body's in every existing compound scene. With it on, the six filter properties below describe this shape alone -- which is how one limb of a ragdoll or one panel of a vehicle can differ from the rest. [method get_filter] reports what the solver holds either way.
Coulomb friction coefficient for this shape alone.

Whether this shape reports hit events (the fast-impact reports behind [signal Box3DWorld.contact_hit]), as an [enum EventMode] tri-state. [constant EVENT_INHERIT] is the default and matches what the body gives its shapes, which is enabled. [method are_hit_events_enabled] reads back what the solver actually holds.

Lets a [Box3DContactRules] one-way rule see this shape's contacts. Only one shape of a pair has to turn it on. Live -- changing it does not rebuild the shape. [b]Only turn this on for a world that has a [member Box3DWorld.contact_rules] table installed.[/b] Box3D's continuous-collision path calls the world's pre-solve callback without a null check, so the flag on a world with no callback registered is a crash during fast motion. Installing a rule table always registers the callback, rules or no rules, which is what makes the flag safe there.
Bounciness of this shape alone. 0 does not bounce.
Resistance to rolling for this shape alone. Only spheres and capsules respond to it.

Whether this shape reports sensor overlap events, as an [enum EventMode] tri-state. [constant EVENT_INHERIT] is the default and matches what the body gives its shapes, which is enabled. [method are_sensor_events_enabled] reads back what the solver actually holds. On a shape of a [b]sensor[/b] body this is what keeps the sensor working at all: Box3D drops every overlap of a sensor whose own shape has sensor events disabled, so [constant EVENT_DISABLED] there is a dead trigger, not a quiet one. On an ordinary body it governs being [i]detected[/i] by other sensors.
Which collider this child contributes, and therefore which size property below applies.
Tessellation of the [constant CYLINDER] and [constant CONE] shapes, which are built as convex hulls.
Radius of the [constant SPHERE] shape, in metres.
Conveyor-belt drive for this shape's surface, in metres per second, in the shape's local space.

Your own tag on this shape's surface material. The solver never reads it, but it rides along on query and hit results -- [method Box3DWorld.raycast]'s [code]user_material[/code] key, [method raycast], [signal Box3DWorld.contact_hit] -- and it reaches the friction and restitution mixing callbacks, which get no other context. 0 unless you author one. This is the per-shape equivalent of the [code]user_material_id[/code] entries in [member Box3DBody.surface_materials], which tag a mesh or height field per triangle instead. [Box3DBody] has no such property of its own: to tag a plain body's collider, give it a [Box3DCollisionShape] child.

constants.constant: A box shape sized by [member box_size].
A sphere shape sized by [member sphere_radius].
A capsule shape sized by [member capsule_radius] and [member capsule_height].
A cylinder, built as a convex hull with [member sides] sides.
A cone with its apex up, built as a convex hull with [member sides] sides.
No live shape: the parent body has not built its shapes yet, or has destroyed them. Returned by [method get_geometry_type] outside a running [Box3DWorld].
A capsule, from [constant CAPSULE]. Read it with [method get_capsule].
A baked compound shape. This node never authors one; it only appears for a shape reached through a query or event payload.
A height field, as authored by [Box3DBody]'s own [constant Box3DBody.HEIGHT_FIELD] shape type. This node never authors one.
A convex hull. [constant BOX], [constant CYLINDER] and [constant CONE] all come back as this too, because Box3D has no separate box, cylinder or cone primitive. Read it with [method get_hull].
A triangle mesh, from [method set_mesh] or from [constant Box3DBody.MESH] on the parent body. No [member shape_type] value produces one. Read it with [method get_mesh].
A sphere, from [constant SPHERE]. Read it with [method get_sphere].

Take whatever the parent [Box3DBody] gives its shapes: contact events follow [member Box3DBody.contact_monitor], sensor and hit events are on. The default, so that adding this property changed no existing scene.

Report this kind of event for this shape whatever the body does. Box3D still ignores the setting where it cannot apply -- sensor events on a shape that is not on a sensor, for instance -- so read the result back with the matching [code]are_*_events_enabled[/code] method.
Do not report this kind of event for this shape, even when the body has it on. The way to keep the decorative shapes of a compound out of a contact-heavy body's event stream.
